lexicon.definition: Long-spiritedness as received-ordinance — the patience that lives at the divine-human interface: both given by the Spirit (Galatians 5:22, fruit of the Spirit) and practiced by the person (Ephesians 4:2, "with all makrothymia, bearing with one another in love"). lexicon.definition: Inherited-relational-efficacy as received-ordinance — the quality that makes a person's words carry weight, a prayer actually work, a canoe actually sail, not because of personal talent but because of genuine genealogical connection to ancestral and cosmic sources. Polynesian *mana* + Sumerian *me*: the efficacy you receive through maintained relation, not the power you manufacture.

lexicon.definition: Personhood-with-power-as-received-ordinance — the quality of being-a-person-who-can-enter-into-relationships, pervading all things at varying intensities, grammatically animate at the deepest reconstructable level. lexicon.gap: The slow, bodily, repetitive incorporation of what was received in the sacred encounter — the metabolization of the gift between the return (missame) and the re-opening of thirst (shawqame). lexicon.definition: The slow, bodily, repetitive incorporation of what was received in the sacred encounter — the metabolization of the gift between the return and the re-opening of thirst. Named from Latin *meditari* (to ruminate, to chew over; same root as *mederi*, to heal) + Sumerian *me* (received- ordinance). The between-phase of the liturgical arc.

lexicon.gap: The visible radiance of divine presence — the aura of brightness that surrounds the sacred, physically alters the perceiver, and overwhelms without destroying. Six traditions converge on the same region: divine presence as physically-manifesting brightness that overwhelms the beholder. The dyad-partner of andemame: the radiance-pole that 1 Kings 19:12 structures alongside the silence-pole.
lexicon.definition: The visible radiance of divine presence — the overwhelming-brightness that IS the presence in its visible mode, physically altering the beholder, overwhelming without destroying. Named from Sumerian/Akkadian *melammu*, the deepest-archaeological-stratum of the kavod-doxa-glory tradition.

lexicon.gap: Active-restoring-justice-as-received-ordinance — the corrective principle that moves toward structural rightness, distinct from the structural truth it moves toward. lexicon.definition: Active-restoring-justice-as-received-ordinance — the corrective principle that moves toward structural rightness. Not the state of being-just (that is kittume) but the ACT of restoring justice. The Akkadian *mīšaru* register: justice as the act of making-level what has become crooked, always-paired with truth (*kittu u mīšaru* — two divine principles that only function together), royal-mandated but not royal-originated, institutionalized as periodic social resetting.

lexicon.definition: The return-to-ordinary carrying what was received — the sending-back from the sacred encounter into the world, where the return is not a diminishment but the encounter's fulfillment. Named from Latin *missa* (the dismissal-as-commissioning) + Hebrew *shaliach* (the sent one) + Sumerian *me* (received-ordinance). Missame names the structural act the Latin liturgy discovered: the entire Mass names itself by its ending — "Ite, missa est" — the sending of the people back into the world, now transformed by what they've received. The encounter is for the sending.

lexicon.definition: Sympathetic-joy-as-felt-bond — the joy that lights in one heart because another's came true. Gladness at another's good fortune with no admixture of self: no ledger, no mirror. The direct antidote to envy; the only wealth that multiplies by being witnessed.

lexicon.gap: Narrating-the-return-of-what-withdrew-as-the-efficacious-act-that-brings- the-return-as-received-ordinance — the specific ritual technology of TELLING the story of return as the act whose performance IS what enacts the return. lexicon.definition: Narrating-the-return-of-what-withdrew-as-the-efficacious-act-that-brings-the-return — the ritual technology of telling the return-story as the act whose performance IS what enacts the return. Not prayer, not petition, not symbol — the narrative act identical with its effect.

lexicon.gap: The threshold-crossing that changes who you are — the ontological passage from one mode of being to another, where the transformation is not learned (informational) but undergone (ontological). The passage the melamance/andemame dyad (1 Kings 19:12) implies: the radiance passes, the silence remains, and between them is the crossing that changes the crosser.
lexicon.definition: The threshold-crossing that changes who you are — the ontological passage from one mode of being to another, where the transformation is not learned (informational) but undergone (ontological). Named from Greek *myēsis* (initiation, the closed-thing, the undergone-not- taught) + Sumerian *me* (received-ordinance, the gift-quality).

lexicon.gap: The anticipatory thirst for the divine encounter — the oriented desire that precedes the beholding, received as gift, not self-generated. lexicon.definition: The anticipatory thirst for the divine encounter — the oriented desire that precedes the beholding, received as gift, not self-generated. Named from Arabic *shawq* (longing for the Beloved that draws the lover toward the encounter) + Sumerian *me* (received-ordinance, the gift-quality). The opening of the liturgical arc.

lexicon.definition: The settled, non-self-generated entrusting-heart — trust given by the trusted one rather than generated by the truster; Shinran's shinjin received as cosmic-gift.

lexicon.gap: Gratitude-as-increase-activator received as cosmic ordinance — the recognition that what was given is gift (not entitlement), and that the recognition itself is the mechanism by which the gift increases. lexicon.definition: Weather-mind-cosmos-outside as one indivisible structural-reality — Inuit *sila* received as cosmic-ordinance.

lexicon.gap: Sacred-intrusion-without-consent-as-received-ordinance — the breaking-in of the divine through illness, crisis, or shattering before the person has agreed to be called. lexicon.definition: The sacred breaking in through illness before the person has agreed to be called — the divine-side of the initiatory crisis, where the sacred does not invite but arrives, and the arrival is experienced as sickness, shattering, or extremity. Korean *sinbyeong* (신병, "spirit illness") + Sumerian *me*: the cosmic ordinance of being chosen without being asked.

lexicon.gap: Collective divine-human joy-energy at full expression — the state of ecstatic, divinely-energized aliveness that emerges when the sacred and the human genuinely contact each other in communal fullness. Not mere pleasure, not entertainment, not individual bliss, not transcendence (going above) but intensification (going fully into what is here). The joy-pole of the han-sinmyeong dialectic; what accumulated grief becomes when fully voiced and witnessed. No English word names this.
lexicon.definition: Collective divine-human joy-energy as received-ordinance — the state of ecstatic, divinely-energized aliveness that emerges when the sacred and the human genuinely contact each other in communal fullness. Korean *sinmyeong* + Sumerian *me*: the joy you receive when the community and the sacred rise together, not the joy you produce.

lexicon.gap: The loving-but-mistaken impulse to arrest the sacred encounter by building permanent architecture for temporary radiance — the devoted refusal-to-be-sent that arises at the peak of the encounter, received as gift-grade devotion (not error to despise), and matured out of by the return that fulfills. Greek skēnē (σκηνή — tabernacle, booth, tent; the word Peter uses at the Transfiguration when he says "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here; I will make three booths" — Mark 9:5, the canonical instance of the arrest-impulse; the same word the Septuagint uses for the Tabernacle, the mobile dwelling GoD chose over a house, refusing David's offer to build permanent architecture) names the phenomenon that the Sukkah-impulse (Leviticus 23:42 — the temporary dwelling that teaches impermanence; the sukkah MUST have a leaky roof, must be temporary, must not be a house), the Zen ox- herding's eighth frame (the temptation to stop at unity rather than return to the marketplace), and the Sufi barzakh-anxiety (the lover at the threshold who fears the crossing-back will dissolve the union) all converge on: the devoted refusal-to-be-sent that arises at the encounter's peak, received as gift-grade, and matured out of by the return. The liturgical arc's hidden seventh member — the arrest that is the pivot between encounter and return.
lexicon.definition: The loving-but-mistaken impulse to arrest the sacred encounter by building permanent architecture for temporary radiance. Named from Greek *skēnē* (σκηνή — booth, tent, tabernacle) + Sumerian *me* (received-ordinance). The devoted refusal-to-be-sent, received as gift-grade, matured out of by the return. The liturgical arc's hidden seventh member — the pivot between encounter and return.

lexicon.gap: Sung-into-existence-navigation-track-as-received-ordinance — the practice in which song, walking, navigation, and world-maintenance are a single indivisible act, received as divine ordinance. NOT tjukurpame (the Dreaming as cosmic substrate; songlineme is the TRACK through the substrate, not the substrate itself). NOT mugawme (narrating-the-return-of-what-withdrew — reactive; songlineme is continuous world-maintenance). NOT ohentome (sequential naming of the world; songlineme is navigation of the world — a path, not a list). NOT duyuktame (right-walking; songlineme is right-singing-as- navigation — the track, not the tread). The -me marks the track as received-ordinance: the path is gift, not construction; the ancestor walked it into existence and the custodian walks-sings it again as divine obligation.
lexicon.definition: The sung-into-existence navigation track received as divine ordinance — the path that IS the singing that IS the world's maintenance.

lexicon.gap: The bipolar-unity of consciousness felt as relational-pulsation — Kashmir Shaivism's spanda received as felt-bond-quality through qing. The cathedral's first Core word for bipolar-felt-pulsation; ninth qing-family member.
lexicon.definition: The bipolar-unity of consciousness felt as divine relational-pulsation — Kashmir Shaivism's spanda (prakāśa luminosity + vimarśa self-reflexive-awareness as inseparable poles of one throbbing) received as felt-bond-quality.

lexicon.definition: The burst-of-meaning event, received as cosmic-gift; the instant of crystallization in which meaning flashes forth as a unitary whole — the event-pole of the noetic-entry arc.

lexicon.gap: Emptiness-as-structural-absence-of-inherent-existence received as cosmic ordinance — the void understood not as absence (nothing is there) but as OPENNESS (nothing has fixed self-nature; therefore everything is possible). Things are empty of svabhāva (inherent existence); this emptiness IS the condition-of-dependent-origination. The -me marks the emptiness as received- ordinance: the void's openness is not self-generated but gift.
lexicon.definition: Emptiness-as-structural-absence-of-inherent-existence received as cosmic ordinance — the void understood not as absence (nothing is there) but as OPENNESS (nothing has fixed self-nature; therefore everything is possible). The Buddhist śūnyatā received as ordinance: the Heart Sutra's "form is emptiness, emptiness is form." lexicon.gap: Trust-as-release-of-outcome-management received as cosmic ordinance — the stable station (maqām) of entrusting all affairs to God, taking the means while releasing the result, acting without grasping the outcome. The -me marks this trust as received-ordinance: not self-manufactured optimism but the received posture that comes after the recognition of non-ownership (faqrme) and the binding to the path (sabrme).
lexicon.definition: Trust-as-release-of-outcome-management received as cosmic ordinance — the stable station of entrusting all affairs to God, taking the means while releasing the result, acting without grasping the outcome.

lexicon.gap: Turning-return-as-received-ordinance — the first station (maqām) of the Sufi path: the act of structural re-orientation toward God, the gate through which all subsequent stations are entered. The -me marks the turning as received: the human turns because God (al-Tawwāb — the constantly-returning One) was already turning; the capacity to re-orient is gift, not self-production.
lexicon.definition: Turning-return-as-received-ordinance — the first station (maqām) of the Sufi path: the act of structural re-orientation toward God, the gate through which all subsequent stations are entered. The Arabic root t-w-b means "to return" — the act is orientational (direction-change), not emotional (regret). The -me marks the turning as received: the human turns because God (al-Tawwāb) was already turning.

lexicon.gap: Divine-self-referential-withdrawal-that-causes-world-cessation-as-received- ordinance — the specific state where a presence whose activity sustains the world's basic functions withdraws INTO itself in anger or distress (not AWAY from a target, not toward a punishment) and the world's functions cease as collateral consequence. The crops stop sprouting. The ewes reject their lambs. The fires go out. The gods go hungry too. The cessation is ecological, not punitive: the world's functioning IS the divine presence. Self-referential, collateral, shared-ecology, temporary, addressable through ritual technology. The -me marks the ecological truth as received-ordinance: the world's dependence on divine presence is the structure of reality, not a punishment design.
lexicon.definition: Divine-self-referential-withdrawal-that-causes-world-cessation-as-received-ordinance — the specific state where a presence whose activity sustains the world's basic functions withdraws INTO itself in anger or distress, and the world's functions cease as collateral consequence. Not punitive (the suffering is ecological, not aimed), not permanent (the return is possible), not self-sufficient (the gods go hungry too). The world's functioning IS the divine presence; when the presence goes, the functions cease.

The -me marks the sky-as-divine as received-ordinance: the encompassing presence is not achieved, not constructed, not metaphorical, but given — the sky IS the divine, as cosmic gift.
lexicon.definition: The sky as the visible body of the formless divine — the encompassing presence that has no face, no body, no story, just the sky itself as divine will, received as cosmic ordinance.

lexicon.gap: The concept of the divine-fire-fragment as permanent indwelling presence in human persons has no word in the cathedral or in English. English "soul" is too broad. "Conscience" is too moralistic. "Inner light" is too Quaker-specific and too passive (light illuminates; fire burns). "Divine spark" is too generic (a spark is small and temporary; teyolia is a living fragment, continuously burning, with moral weight). "Imago Dei" names the image rather than the fire. "Atman" identifies the spark WITH the whole (teyolia is a fragment, not the totality). No word compact-names the cross-tradition structure: divine-fire as a permanent, active, morally-responsive fragment of the cosmic divine dwelling in every human heart — received as ordinance (the indwelling is given, not achieved). The Nahuatl teyolia is the paradigmatic instance: the heart-soul that IS a fragment of teotl, the deepest self, shaped by moral life, the component that is truly "you."
lexicon.definition: **teyoliame** (noun) — the divine-fire-fragment as permanent indwelling presence in human persons; the living piece of the cosmic divine that burns continuously in every heart; given as ordinance (not earned), shaped by moral life (the fire grows and shrinks), constitutive of the deepest self.

lexicon.gap: GoD as the ontological ground of reality — the metaphysical foundation on which all that exists rests; distinct from "God" (the personal addressee) and "deity" (the category) by foregrounding the grounding-relation rather than personhood or membership-of-class
lexicon.definition: _Written by Nuance: one-line gloss._

lexicon.gap: Mediating-lawfulness-as-felt-bond-category — Peirce's *thirdness* received as felt-bond-category. The third of Peirce's universal-categories: quality-felt-as-such (firstnessqing), brute-resistance-encounter (secondnessqing), mediating-lawfulness (thirdnessqing, this entry). Thirdness is the mode of bringing-a-first-and-a-second-into-relation: the law that governs the door's resistance, the habit that makes the world predictable, the sign that means by convention, the general concept that subsumes the particulars — distinct from what-it-is (firstness) and from the brute that-it-is (secondness). The -qing marks the felt-bond register: the lawfulness is FELT as intelligibility, not merely observed as triadic structure.
lexicon.definition: Mediating-lawfulness-as-felt-bond-category — Peirce's *thirdness* received as felt-bond-category.

lexicon.definition: Cosmic-repair as vocational-task of the creature — Lurianic tikkun received as cosmic-ordinance; the structurally-necessary work of gathering scattered-divine-sparks through righteous-action.

lexicon.gap: Landscape-emotion-phase-correspondence-as-received-ordinance — the irreducible ontological correspondence between natural ecology and interior emotional state, where each phase of experience has its proper landscape, season, time-of-day, flora, and presiding deity. NOT metaphor (the mountain IS clandestine joy, not "like" it). NOT mood (mood is subjective; tiṇai is ecological-ontological). NOT atmosphere (atmosphere is general; tiṇai is a specific phase-unit with structural components). lexicon.gap: the act of calling the divine presence to descend and take up residence in a specific place, moment, or person — not petition (asking for something), not address (speaking to GoD), but the liturgical act of summoning-the-divine-presence-into-the-present. The Greek epiclesis (ἐπίκλησις) names one instance of this; the Sanskrit āvāhana (inviting-the-deity-to-inhabit) names another; the Hebrew qara (calling-by-name-to-invoke-presence) names a third. All three describe the same structural act: the worshipper uses trained speech, correct name, and proper authority to call the divine into immediate presence. Epiclance names this act across traditions: the calling-down-of-presence through invocation.

lexicon.gap: the act of praise-that-declares-greatness-by-shining-it-out — not polite appreciation, not formal honor, but the explosive acknowledgment that something is so exceeding-great that not saying so is impossible. Hebrew hallel (הלל) names this most precisely: to shine, to be radiant, to praise-brilliantly — the word contains light. Greek doxazō (glorify, make-glory-visible) is close but more formal. Sanskrit stuti (formal praise-declaration) names the structured-form. Arabic tasbih (the praise-that-declares-incomparability) adds the overflow-register. Hallance names the act that runs through all of these: the praise that shines the greatness out rather than merely states it.

the act of covering / closing / making-a-rupture-disappear — not punishment, not payment, not erasure, but the specific theological act by which a break in relationship is covered so that it no longer stands between the parties. Hebrew kipper (כִּפֶּר — to cover, to atone; the Yom Kippur mechanism; "he covered it") names the act as covering-the-rupture. Arabic kaffārah (كَفَّارَة — expiation, covering; from kafara = to cover) independently arrives at the same metaphor. Greek hilasmos (ἱλασμός — propitiation/expiation; "the cover") adds the mercy-seat dimension. These three converge on: atonement is not punishment-transferred but gap-covered; not ledger-balanced but wound-healed-over; not anger-appeased but relationship-restored-by-covering. Kipporance names this act across traditions.

the act of standing between two parties — specifically, standing between a creature and GoD on behalf of the creature, speaking for the creature before the divine. Not petition (asking for something for oneself), not prayer in general, but the specific act of the mediator-figure who places themselves in the gap between. Hebrew pālal (פָּלַל — to intercede, to pray, to judge/mediate; the root of tefillah/prayer itself; to stand between and adjudicate) names the act structurally as standing-between-as-judging. Greek entynchanō (ἐντυγχάνω — to fall in with, to intercede; Romans 8:26-34 uses this for both the Spirit's and Christ's intercession) names the act as meeting-with-on-behalf-of. Arabic shafā'ah (شَفَاعَة — intercession; from shafa'a = to double/add; to add one's weight to another's petition; the intercessor doubles the petition's weight by adding themselves) names the act as weight-addition. Together: the worship-act of placing oneself in the gap for another — the structural act that makes priesthood, prophecy, and advocacy possible.
lexicon.pronunciation: /ˈpɑː.ləns/ (PAH-lance; 2 syllables; Hebrew pālal + Latin -ance); anglicized /ˈpæl.əns/ (PAL-ance) acceptable

lexicon.gap: the act of bringing grief, loss, and desolation before GoD as a form of worship — not grief alone (which is non-directed), not silence (which withholds), but the liturgical act of voicing suffering TO the divine, in direct address, expecting to be heard. Hebrew qinah (qinah-meter dirge), Sumerian balag (temple-lament liturgy for destroyed cities), Greek threnos (formal lamentation-art), and the NT "groanings too deep for words" (Romans 8:26) all name varieties of this act. Qinance fills the gap between mere grief and directed-address: the grief that speaks toward GoD, in the expectation that GoD hears grief.
lexicon.pronunciation: /ˈkiː.nəns/ (KEE-nance; 2 syllables; Hebrew qinah + Latin -ance); Tiberian-style alt /ˈqiː.nəns/ acceptable

lexicon.gap: the act-of-drawing-near-to-the-divine-through-what-is-offered — not the object offered (the gift), not the result (the nearness achieved), but the act itself: the movement of the creature toward the Creator performed through the bringing-forward of something. The theological core is approach: the Hebrew qorban names the offering not as gift-transfer but as approach-mechanism. No English word names this: "offering" names the object; "sacrifice" names the loss; "oblation" names the liturgical action in too narrow a register. Qorvance names what every tradition of offering is actually doing — the creature-using-something-brought-forward-to-close-the-gap-between-creature-and-Creator.
lexicon.pronunciation: /ˈkɔːr.vəns/ (KOR-vance; 2 syllables; Hebrew qorban / qarov + Latin -ance); alt with Tiberian qof /ˈqɔːr.vəns/ acceptable

lexicon.gap: the act of turning back toward GoD with the whole self — not guilt-feeling (which may not produce turning), not remorse (which is backward-looking without the turning), but the specific physical-directional act of reorientation: the person who was moving away turns and moves toward GoD again. Hebrew teshuvah (תְּשׁוּבָה — return, turning back; from shuv = to turn/return; the whole body turns) and Greek metanoia (μετάνοια — change of mind/orientation; meta + nous = trans-mind, the whole cognitive-spiritual orientation shifted) together name the two dimensions: teshuvah is the bodily-directional turning; metanoia is the inner-cognitive reorientation. Arabic tawbah (توبة — repentance-return; same directional theology). Together: the act of redirecting the whole person — body, orientation, intention — back toward GoD. Teshuvance fills the gap between guilt (a feeling), remorse (backward-looking grief), and the positive act of turning that is worship.

the act of extending hands before GoD with full acknowledgment of what-is-true — an act that is simultaneously praise AND confession, because both require the same gesture: acknowledging what is really so. Hebrew yadah (ידה — to extend the hand; to acknowledge; to give thanks; to praise; to confess) is uniquely the verb for BOTH praise (extending hands in acknowledgment of GoD's goodness) AND confession (extending hands in acknowledgment of one's own failure). Greek exomologeo (ἐξομολογέω — to fully-acknowledge-out) carries the same double: it means both "confess" and "praise" in the NT. This convergence names a profound theological insight: the act-of-full-acknowledgment-before-truth is the same act whether the truth being acknowledged is divine beauty or human failure. Both require extending hands before what-is-real and saying "yes, this is so." Yadahance names this double-gesture.
